title: Instrumentation sprint checklist for model cold-starts and dashboard bake-off
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is the sprint-level checklist for instrumenting, validating, and shipping a minimal set of metrics/traces and dashboard panels focused on model cold-start behavior (first-requests, KV-cache fills, model load spikes). Goal is to have a compact operator dashboard + a short runbook so oncall can quickly triage and engineers can measure regressions during model rollouts.

High-level goals (MVP):
- Define 6 core metrics (names, type, unit, rationale).
- Add 6 trace annotations to capture cross-service latency breakdown for first-in-session requests.
- Ship a dashboard with 8 panels: 3 latency slices, 2 cache-warmth visualizations, 2 error/queue panels, 1 rollout-impact heatmap.
- Add lightweight alerts (noisy-resistance) and a one-page runbook for the oncall.

Intended audience:
Operator teams (SRE/ops), runtime engineers (serving-runtime), platform (routing/policies), and product engineers running canaries.

Core metric definitions (MVP):
1) inference.first_request_latency_p50/p95/p99
- Type: histogram-derived quantiles
- Unit: ms
- Rationale: capture user-perceived latency for the very first token request in a session or after model swap.
- How to compute: restrict to requests where trace.tag.session_request_index == 0 or request.meta.first_request=true.
- Owner: Devon Brooks (serving-runtime).

2) kvcache.fill_rate
- Type: counter (increments per KV-cache fill event) + rate per minute
- Unit: fills/minute and fills/issued-request percentage (derived)
- Rationale: quantify how often we are performing cache loads during cold starts which correlates to longer latency and GPU memory churn.
- Owner: Grace Huang (applied-ml instrument).

3) kvcache.warmth_index
- Type: gauge (0..1) with decay window (exponential moving average over 5m)
- Unit: ratio
- Rationale: operator-facing indicator of how "warm" a model-serving pool is for a tenant/workload. Not exact: used for trend and alerting.
- Instrumentation note: emit per-pool and per-tenant.

4) model.load_duration_ms
- Type: summary/histogram
- Unit: ms
- Rationale: time to load model artifact into GPU memory or attach weights to runner. Crucial for Private/Dedicated deployments.
- Emit: start at model load triggered, emit at load complete or failure.

5) schedule.queue_length_by_pool
- Type: gauge
- Unit: number of queued jobs
- Rationale: detect scheduling/backpressure during cold waves when autoscaler hasn't spun up capacity.

6) request.retries_by_cause
- Type: counter with label (cause = timeout|oom|service-unavailable)
- Rationale: increase in retries on first-request path points to cold-start-related instability rather than model quality regressions.

Trace annotations / span conventions (MVP):
- Add these semantic tags to root span for easier backtraces: session_id, session_request_index, model_variant, pool_id, cache_fill_hint (true/false), rollout_tag.
- Ensure spans cover: client-proxy (ingest), router/decision, scheduler/queue, model-loader (artifact load), runner/execution, kvcache/fill, responder/stream.
- Example quicktrace: root -> router -> scheduler(queued) -> model-loader(load) -> runner(exec) -> kvcache(fill) -> responder.
- Sampling guideline: sample 100% of first-request sessions (session_request_index==0) and 0.5% of steady-state to keep cost bounded.

Dashboard layout guidance (operator-first):
Top row (single pane width):
- Global first_request_latency p50/95 sparkline (multi-tenant heatmap selector).
- Model-load-duration median + recent histogram.
Second row (two-thirds + one-third):
- Left (2/3): KV-cache warmth index by pool (stacked heatmap across tenants) + per-tenant selector.
- Right (1/3): Queue length by pool (bar chart) with alert band overlay.
Third row (three panels):
- Retry rate by cause (stacked area)
- Cache fill rate vs request rate (dual axis)
- Cold-start impact: canary vs production latency delta heatmap (rows=canaries, cols=time bucket)
Bottom row (compact):
- Recent sampled traces list (clickable to trace viewer) filtered to session_request_index==0.
- Known-issue banner (editable) where SRE can pin current suspected regressions.

Alert rules (starter set, avoid flapping):
- A1: model.load_duration_ms p95 > 10s for > 5m AND queue_length_by_pool > 5 -> Pager (possible infra stall)
- A2: kvcache.warmth_index < 0.25 for a pool for > 10m -> Page to SRE (investigate rollout/evictions)
- A3: inference.first_request_latency_p95_increase >= 2x baseline over 15m but p50 stable -> Page to runtime owners (regression on long-tailed cold starts)
- A4: request.retries_by_cause increases by >200% relative to 1h baseline -> Slack alert (ops) with recent traces linked.

Runbook sketch (one-pager):
- Step 0: Check dashboard filters: pool_id, model_variant, tenant.
- Step 1: If A1 -> inspect model.load_duration_ms histogram; open last sampled trace that had model-loader span; look for OOM or file system latency.
- Step 2: If A2 -> check autoscaler logs, eviction events, and recent rollout_tag changes. Consider warmup policy if rolling out a new quantized model.
- Step 3: If A3 -> compare canary vs prod heatmap; see if rollout_tag correlates; rollback canary or increase burst capacity to mitigate.
- Step 4: If A4 -> inspect request.retries_by_cause label and correlate with trace kvcache.fill events.

Sprint instrumentation checklist (actionable tasks):
- [ ] Add metric emits for inference.first_request_latency and ensure root-level request.meta.first_request is set by proxy layer. (Owner: Liam O'Connor)
- [ ] Emit kvcache.fill events and attach pool_id + tenant_id labels. (Owner: Grace Huang)
- [ ] Implement kvcache.warmth_index calculation in telemetry service (EMA 5m). Add per-pool and per-tenant shards. (Owner: Grace)
- [ ] Add model.load_duration_ms events in model-manager; include failure reasons (checksum_mismatch, oom, missing-artifact). (Owner: Devon Brooks)
- [ ] Add trace-span for model-loader and mark spans with rollout_tag, model_variant. (Owner: Devon)
- [ ] Dashboard panels: build initial layout in observability dashboard repo and link to runbook. (Owner: Asha Patel)
- [ ] Alert rules + suppression windows, add escalation policy and test noise. (Owner: SRE lead)
- [ ] End-to-end test: simulate cold-start by invalidating pool warmth and measuring end-to-end trace capture. Create a test canary job (CI). (Owner: QA)
- [ ] Add docs snippet to onboarding for new models: how to verify cold-start telemetry. (Owner: Developer Experience)

Acceptance criteria for the sprint:
- All 6 core metrics are emitted with labels documented in the telemetry schema.
- Dashboard exists in the observability repo and renders for at least 3 pools and one tenant.
- Sampling rules implemented so 100% of first-request traces are captured for 48h in dev canary (cost amortized to dev cluster).
- One runbook page linked from dashboard and tested in a tabletop drill.
- No pager storms during 2-day after-ship window (suppression thresholds in place).

Open questions / design tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How expensive will capturing 100% of first-request traces be at scale? We probably need dynamic sampling with a global budget plus tenant carve-outs for enterprise customers.
- Should kvcache.warmth_index be per-model or per-runner? Per-pool seems a good compromise but loses per-model granularity for multi-model pools.
- How to correlate cold-starts to backing storage latency (S3/EFS)? Add model-artifact-fetch-duration span or rely on model.load_duration_ms with labels? Prefer explicit span.
- UX: do we show absolute numbers or normalize per-request? Operators have asked for both; keep a dual-axis cache fill rate vs request rate panel.

Quick links and references:
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Cold+Start+Playbook
- Telemetry schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/187
- Run a drill ticket: JIRA-OBS-3421

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; we want a minimal ship that enables rapid iterations. Please call out missing labels you need for correlating tenant traffic.
- If you think an additional metric is critical for your team (e.g., FS latency per artifact fetch), add it as a subtask with owner.

Last checked: 2024-12-05 by Asha Patel

(Informal scratchpad below — keep while drafting, can be removed before final):
- TODO: decide exact decay window for warmth_index (try 5m EMA first).
- TODO: sample budget config: 100% first-request for dev, 5% for prod initially then tune.
- Quick experiment: run small-scale invalidation of KV cache on staging and capture the differential in p95 first_request_latency (expected > 2x).
